newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 20.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Daewoo Avia, which is currently the largest domestic producer of medium-sized freight vehicles, wants to double its production by the year 2000. Skoda Liaz and Tatra, the second largest producers, are preparing radical restructuring including modernisation of their products.

- The proposal for a new law for pension insurance, which the cabinet should address on Wednesday, will also be discussed in a parliament meeting in February along with a proposal from the Social Democratic Party (CSSD).

- Monetary institutions have less than half a year to comply with new Czech National Bank regulations, effective from the beginning of this year, to give evidence of their provisions in line with their portfolios of stocks and bonds.
- Contrasting opinions are crystalising among Czech politicians before tomorrow's signing of the Czech-German Declaration during German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's visit to Prague.

- While year-on-year inflation during the first half of this year should be around 7.5 percent, deregulation of housing, energy and gas prices in July, together with the possible increase in VAT charges for energy and fuel, could lead to year-on-year inflation of more than 10 percent.

PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel announced on television on Sunday that some of the documents concerning the secret service (BIS) which chairman of the representative parliament Milos Zeman gave him last week could possibly give reason for suspicion of illegal activities.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Czech Railways, which has long been loss-making, and has had problems with requests for lower service prices and scant investment possibilities, could go through another economic shock within the next few years. If the company is not able to quickly obtain a large variety of new freight wagons to fit the EC's demands, it could lose a large part of its profits.

LIDOVE NOVINY - French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette stated that France would like the Czech Republic to enter into the European Community as soon as possible, and confirmed the validity of President Chirac's promise to do all he can to ensure membership by 2000.
